title: Conditional non-Hermitian acceleration of multiphoton atomic transitions
authors: Marcos V. S. de Paula, Alexandre P. Costa, A. V. Dodonov
abstract: Continuous monitoring can convert a dissipative channel into a resource for accelerating otherwise slow multiphoton transitions. We consider a three-level atom in a $Λ$ configuration and condition the evolution on the absence of photon emission through an auxiliary monitored decay channel. The resulting no-jump dynamics is governed by a non-Hermitian Rabi-type Hamiltonian. Using Floquet theory and Brillouin--Wigner projection-operator perturbation method, we derive effective two-state descriptions of odd-multiphoton resonances in the semiclassical and quantum Rabi models. The effective population-transfer rate, defined as the inverse of the time required for the first complete transfer between the atomic states, is maximized at an exceptional point, where its enhancement factor approaches $π/2$, corresponding to an approximately $57\%$ increase over the Hermitian value. Numerical results for three- and five-photon resonances closely reproduce the analytical transition times and yield non-negligible postselection probabilities. By contrast, the complete unconditioned dissipative evolution does not exhibit the same population-transfer enhancement. These results demonstrate a speed--success trade-off for measurement-conditioned multiphoton state transfer.
summary: The research demonstrates that continuous monitoring of an auxiliary decay channel can significantly accelerate slow multiphoton transitions in three-level atoms. By deriving effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians and applying perturbation theory, the authors show this acceleration is achieved only within the measured (no-jump) ensemble, leading to a quantifiable speedup compared to standard dissipative evolution.
main_problem: The paper investigates how continuous monitoring of a dissipative channel can accelerate otherwise slow multiphoton atomic transitions.
main_result: Conditioning the evolution on no photon emission accelerates the transition rate, achieving an enhancement factor approaching $\pi/2$ (a ~57% increase) compared to the unconditioned dynamics.
method: The authors use Floquet theory and Brillouin–Wigner projection-operator perturbation methods to derive effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonians for both semiclassical and quantum Rabi models.
model_or_system: The system is a three-level atom in a $\Lambda$ configuration driven by a classical field. The dynamics are analyzed using a conditioned master equation derived from the full dissipative evolution, leading to an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Effective population-transfer rate (inverse time for first complete transfer), probability of successful postselection ($P_c$), and the enhancement factor of the transition rate.
important_parameters: Odd-multiphoton resonance conditions ($\Omega \approx (2K+1)\omega$); coupling strengths ($g, g_f$) and decay rates ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as neglecting weak unmonitored dissipation channels and the nonresonant auxiliary level $|fangle$ during analytical derivations.
figures_summary: Figures compare semiclassical and full quantum Rabi model dynamics for three-photon and five-photon resonances, contrasting conditioned (no-jump) evolution with unconditional dissipative evolution regarding populations and transfer rates.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the non-Hermitian dynamics via continuous monitoring, then applies perturbation theory to derive effective two-state Hamiltonians. Finally, it compares analytical solutions derived from these models against direct numerical integration for both semiclassical and full quantum regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems by showing how measurement backaction (monitoring) can be harnessed as a resource to engineer faster state transfer rates in cavity QED or atomic physics settings, while quantifying the associated speed-success trade-off.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Level scheme of the monitored Λ-atom. The resonant odd- multiphoton transition couples |g⟩and |e⟩, while the auxiliary state |f⟩is popu- lated through a weak dispersive interaction and the monitored decay |e⟩→|f⟩. The conditioned dynamics is obtained by postselecting trajectories in which no quantum jump associated with this incoherent decay channel occurs.

Figure 2: Semiclassical Rabi model at the three-photon resonance. (a) Ground- state population for the initial state |e⟩under Hermitian evolution; the black and red curves are the numerical and analytical results, respectively. (b) Ground- state population in the conditioned no-jump dynamics. The first analytical and numerical transfer maxima occur at essentially the same time and earlier than in panel (a). (c) Probability of no jump during the interval [0, t). (d) Atomic pop- ulations in the unconditioned dissipative evolution generated by the complete master equation (solved numerically).

Figure 3: Same quantities as in Fig. 2, but for the five-photon resonance. The horizontal axis spans a longer time interval because the five-photon transition is intrinsically slower, even though a larger coupling strength is used.

Figure 4: Quantum Rabi model at the three-photon resonance. (a) Population of the vacuum Fock state |0⟩: numerical Hermitian dynamics (black), analytical Hermitian dynamics (red), numerical conditioned dynamics (blue), and analyt- ical conditioned dynamics (orange). (b) Population of the Fock state |3⟩. (c) Atomic ground-state population Pg. (d) Mean photon number. (e) Probability of no jump during [0, t). (f) Atomic populations and mean photon number in the unconditioned dissipative evolution generated by the complete master equation.
Figure 5: Same quantities as in Fig. 4, but at the five-photon resonance. Panel (b) shows the population of the Fock state |5⟩.
